time._notes: Clock speed lives in living.day_seconds (real seconds per game day at 1x); 3x and 10x divide it.

attendance._notes: M2.6: base_demand 60 -> 72 (+20%). Elasticity 0.35 -> 0.6 with a new price_penalty_exponent of 2 (M2.6 playtest-2 fix): at 0.35 a $20 ticket earned as much as a $5 one, so the overspend trap paid for itself. Overcharging is now penalised by the SQUARE of the overcharge, so ticket revenue peaks near $7-8 and collapses above it: a $20 ticket empties the park (0.5% of demand) instead of paying as well as $5 did. Satisfaction (restrooms, tour guides) softens the curve, so investing in visitors is what buys the right to charge more. The reference price is unaffected (priceFactor(reference) = 1), so the classic $5 opening is unchanged. empty_park_factor 0.25 -> 0.15: a park with no living dinosaurs pulls a trickle of visitors and cannot cover its own costs. Cleanliness decay per day = cleanliness_decay_per_day x clamp(attendance / cleanliness_decay_ref_attendance, min_factor, max_factor): an empty park barely gets dirty, a packed one needs more maintenance.

living._notes: dino_label_always lists the sizes whose pens always carry a name chip (all three: an unlabelled blob is unreadable); other pens still label on hover. day_seconds is THE clock: one game day at 1x takes this many real seconds (M2.6: 6). 3x/10x run proportionally faster; agents cap at max_speed_factor.

parcel._notes: space_per_tile x parcel tile count = enclosure capacity in space units. area_factor scales biome plot_cost by tile count (sub-linear: big parcels are a modest per-tile discount); counts missing from the table use count ^ area_factor_exponent. Fence cost = per segment x outline edges (tile edges not shared inside the parcel).

events._notes: pause_at_speed_max: at game speeds above this, non-critical events go to the ticker and the daily digest instead of a modal. pause_kinds: event effect kinds that always open a modal (plus foreclosure, win milestones and the Quarterly Report, which are not events). 'starving' is the daily starving-dinosaur warning: an asset about to die pauses the clock even at 10x.
